1.6 Budget and Procurement
Routine consumables (e.g., line paint, filters, lubricants) shall be ordered through the Facilities Manager. Capital replacements require a separate proposal to the Facilities Committee. No contractor work shall commence without a purchase order number, except in a genuine emergency where the Facilities Manager may authorise work verbally, confirmed in writing within two working days.

---

SECTION 2 – SAFETY PROCEDURES

2.1 General Safety
All personnel shall comply with the Health and Safety at Work etc. Act 1974 and Club safety policies. Personal protective equipment (PPE) appropriate to the task shall be worn. A PPE inventory is maintained by the Facilities Manager.

2.2 Working at Height
- Ladders shall be inspected before use and must have a current inspection tag.
- Work above 2 metres requires a second person present unless a mobile elevating work platform (MEWP) is used.
- MEWP operation is restricted to certified operators. A current certificate list is held in the club office.

2.3 Chemical Handling
Herbicides, pesticides, and cleaning chemicals shall be stored in the locked store adjacent to the maintenance shed. Material safety data sheets are kept in the store and in the club office. Mixing and application shall follow manufacturer instructions. Spill kits are located at the store and in the grounds vehicle.

2.4 Electrical Safety
- Portable electrical equipment shall be PAT tested annually. Stickers shall record the test date.
- Fixed installations shall be inspected by a qualified electrician every five years, or sooner if there is reason to doubt safety.
- No unauthorised modification of electrical circuits is permitted.

2.5 Lone Working
Grounds staff shall not operate machinery (e.g., mowers, strimmers, irrigation pumps) while alone on the premises outside normal club hours. A check-in procedure with the Facilities Manager or duty officer is required.

2.6 Accident Reporting
All accidents and near misses shall be recorded in the Accident Book (kept in the club office) and reported to the Facilities Manager. RIDDOR-reportable incidents shall be notified to the enforcing authority by the Facilities Manager within the statutory timescale.

SECTION 4 – EXTERNAL CONTRACTORS

4.1 Approved Contractors
The Facilities Committee maintains a list of approved contractors for specialist work (e.g., court resurfacing, boiler servicing, tree surgery). Only contractors on this list shall be engaged, unless a specific exception is approved by the Facilities Manager.
5.3.2 Monthly (all courts)

- Inspect surface for cracks, lifting, or surface deterioration. Record any defects in the Exception Log with a photograph.
- Check court surrounds, including fencing, gates, and net posts, for damage or loose fixings.
- Lubricate gate hinges and net post mechanisms with a light oil.
- Inspect court signage (e.g., court booking rules, no-cycle signs) and replace as necessary.

5.3.3 Quarterly (all courts)

- Remove moss and algae using an approved biocide, following manufacturer’s instructions. Do not apply biocide within 48 hours of a forecast of heavy rain.
- Check surface level for depressions or raised areas. Use a straightedge and level; record any deviation greater than 5 mm in the Exception Log.
- Inspect expansion joints; report any joint that has opened beyond 10 mm.

5.3.4 Annual (all courts)

- In September, carry out a full surface inspection and prepare a condition report for the Facilities Committee. The report shall include photographs, measurements of any defects, and a recommendation for resurfacing or repair.

5.4.1 Resurfacing Procedure

- At least six months before the planned resurfacing date, the Facilities Manager shall commission a condition survey from an approved contractor.
- The Facilities Manager shall prepare a specification of works, including surface preparation, any crack repairs, and the number of coats of surface dressing.
- At least three months before the planned start date, the Facilities Manager shall obtain quotations from at least two approved contractors.
- The Facilities Committee shall approve the contractor and the budget at a meeting no later than two months before the planned start date.
- The club shall notify members of the resurfacing dates at least four weeks in advance, via the club noticeboard and website.
- Courts shall be closed from the start of the works until the contractor certifies that the surface is ready for play. The Facilities Manager shall record the closure dates in the Exception Log.

5.4.2 Post-Resurfacing Inspection

Within 14 days of completion of resurfacing works, the Facilities Manager shall inspect the court with the contractor and agree a snagging list. The snagging list shall be completed by the contractor within 28 days. A final inspection shall be carried out by the Facilities Manager before the court is reopened.

5.5 Line Marking

- Line markings shall be checked weekly during the playing season (April to September) and repainted as necessary.
- Markings shall be repainted in full at the start of each season, using a tennis-specific line paint.
- The Facilities Manager shall ensure that the paint colour matches the existing court colour and that markings comply with LTA regulations.

5.6 Nets and Posts
- Visual inspection of the roof covering from ground level and, where safe access is available, from the roof itself. Binoculars shall be used for areas not readily accessible from ground level.
- Inspection of gutters and downpipes for blockages, leaks, and signs of corrosion. Gutters shall be cleared of leaves and debris at each inspection.
- Inspection of flashing, soakers, and abutments for signs of lifting, cracking, or separation from the wall or roof surface.
- Inspection of roof tiles or slates for cracks, slips, or missing units. Any displaced tiles or slates shall be noted and made safe if there is a risk of falling.
- Inspection of the roof structure from the inside of the clubhouse, including the roof void where accessible. Checks shall include signs of water staining, dampness, or daylight visible through the roof covering.
- Inspection of any roof-mounted equipment, including aerials and solar panels, for security of fixing and signs of damage.
- Inspection of the condition of any roof access hatches and of the ladder or steps used to reach the roof.

Any defects identified during the inspection shall be recorded in the Facilities Log and reported to the Facilities Committee at its next meeting. Defects that present an immediate risk to safety or that are likely to cause significant water damage shall be reported to the Facilities Manager immediately and, where necessary, made safe without delay.

**5.7.4 General Provisions for Roof Works**

- All roof works shall be carried out by an approved contractor.

- The clubhouse shall not be occupied during roof works that involve the removal of large sections of the roof covering.

- The Facilities Manager shall record all roof works in the Facilities Log, including the date of the works, the name of the contractor, and a summary of the works carried out.
**5.8 Irrigation System**

**5.8.1 General**

The irrigation system serves the following areas: the main square, the practice nets, the bowling green surrounds, and the flower beds adjacent to the clubhouse. The system is a fully automated pop-up sprinkler system with a central controller located in the equipment store. Water is supplied from the mains via a dedicated metered connection.

The purpose of this section is to define the procedures for the seasonal startup and shutdown of the irrigation system, and to specify the routine maintenance required to keep the system in good working order. All work on the irrigation system shall be carried out by the Facilities Manager or an approved contractor. The Facilities Manager shall keep a record of all irrigation system work in the Facilities Log, including the date, the nature of the work, and the name of any contractor involved.

**5.8.2 Seasonal Startup – Spring**

The system shall be started up each year in April, or as soon as the risk of frost has passed. The Facilities Manager shall determine the appropriate date based on the weather forecast. The startup procedure shall be carried out as follows:

1.  **Inspect the controller.** Check that the controller is functioning correctly and that the battery back-up is in good condition. Replace the battery if necessary.
2.  **Open the main isolation valve.** The valve is located in the valve box adjacent to the equipment store. Open the valve slowly to avoid water hammer.
3.  **Pressurise the system.** Once the main valve is open, allow the system to pressurise. Check all visible pipework and connections for leaks.
4.  **Check the backflow preventer.** The backflow preventer shall be tested by an approved contractor at least once every two years. The test shall be recorded in the Facilities Log.
5.  **Inspect the sprinkler heads.** Walk the entire system and check each sprinkler head. Remove any debris, soil, or grass clippings from around the heads. Replace any damaged or missing heads.
6.  **Adjust the spray patterns.** Adjust the sprinkler heads so that they water the intended areas only. Avoid watering paths, fences, or the clubhouse building.
7.  **Set the controller programme.** Set the controller to the appropriate watering schedule for the time of year. The schedule shall be adjusted to account for rainfall. Watering shall not take place during periods of heavy rain.
8.  **Run a manual test.** Run each zone manually for a short period to confirm that the system is operating correctly. Check that each zone is pressurising and that the sprinkler heads are popping up and retracting properly.

**5.8.3 Seasonal Shutdown – Autumn**

The system shall be shut down each year in October, or as soon as the risk of frost is imminent. The Facilities Manager shall determine the appropriate date based on the weather forecast. The shutdown procedure shall be carried out as follows:

1.  **Drain the system.** The system is fitted with drain valves at the lowest points of the pipework. Open all drain valves and allow the system to drain completely.
2.  **Blow out the system.** Using an air compressor, blow out any remaining water from the pipework. This is essential to prevent frost damage to the pipes and sprinkler heads. The compressor shall be connected to the system via the drain valve fitting.
3.  **Close the main isolation valve.** Once the system is drained, close the main isolation valve.
4.  **Insulate exposed pipework.** Any pipework that is above ground and could be exposed to frost shall be insulated.
5.  **Protect the controller.** The controller shall be protected from damp and cold. The battery shall be removed and stored in a warm, dry place.
6.  **Record the shutdown.** The date of the shutdown shall be recorded in the Facilities Log.
**6. EMERGENCY PROCEDURES AND URGENT REPAIRS**

**6.1 General Principles**

The procedures in this Section apply when there is an immediate risk to health and safety, a risk of significant damage to club property, or a failure that prevents the club from operating. In all cases, the safety of members, visitors, and staff takes precedence over the protection of buildings and equipment.

Where an emergency occurs outside normal working hours, the Facilities Manager shall be contacted in the first instance. If the Facilities Manager cannot be reached, the Club Secretary shall be contacted. The duty of any staff member or volunteer who discovers an emergency is to make the situation safe where it is safe to do so, and then to report the matter without delay.

The Facilities Manager shall maintain a list of approved contractors for emergency call-outs. This list is reproduced at Section 6.6. The list shall be reviewed annually and updated whenever a contractor's details change.

**6.2 Gas Leak or Suspected Gas Leak**

If a gas leak is suspected, or if there is a strong smell of gas in or near the clubhouse, the following procedure shall be followed:

1.  Do not operate any electrical switches, including light switches, and do not use a mobile phone inside the building.
2.  Open doors and windows to ventilate the area.
3.  Turn off the gas supply at the meter, if it is safe to do so. The meter is located in the external cupboard on the north wall of the clubhouse.
4.  Leave the building immediately.
5.  Telephone the National Gas Emergency Service on **0800 111 999**. Give the operator the club's address and postcode (The Pavilion, Green Lane, Melton Mowbray, LE13 0JZ) and state that the building is a sports clubhouse.
6.  Do not re-enter the building until it has been declared safe by the emergency service or a Gas Safe registered engineer.

**6.3 Fire**

All staff and volunteers shall be familiar with the fire evacuation procedure, which is displayed on the noticeboard in the main hall and in the kitchen. The procedure is summarised below.

1.  Raise the alarm by shouting "FIRE" and operating the nearest break-glass alarm point.
2.  Evacuate the building by the nearest available exit. Do not stop to collect personal belongings.
3.  Assemble at the designated assembly point, which is the far side of the car park, by the main gate.
4.  The Duty Officer or senior staff member present shall check that the building is clear, if it is safe to do so.
5.  Telephone the Fire Service on **999** from a safe location. State the address clearly.
6.  Do not re-enter the building for any reason until the Fire Service has confirmed that it is safe.

Fire extinguishers are located in the following positions: one in the main hall, one in the kitchen, one in the ground floor corridor, and one in the upstairs storeroom. Extinguishers shall be checked monthly by the Clubhouse Maintenance Team and serviced annually by the approved contractor.

**6.5.1 Power Failure**

SECTION 2 – SAFETY PROCEDURES

2.1 General Safety
All personnel shall comply with the Health and Safety at Work etc. Act 1974 and Club safety policies. Personal protective equipment (PPE) appropriate to the task shall be worn. A PPE inventory is maintained by the Facilities Manager.

2.2 Working at Height
- Ladders shall be inspected before use and must have a current inspection tag.
- Work above 2 metres requires a second person present unless a mobile elevating work platform (MEWP) is used.
- MEWP operation is restricted to certified operators. A current certificate list is held in the club office.

2.3 Chemical Handling
Herbicides, pesticides, and cleaning chemicals shall be stored in the locked store adjacent to the maintenance shed. Material safety data sheets are kept in the store and in the club office. Mixing and application shall follow manufacturer instructions. Spill kits are located at the store and in the grounds vehicle.

2.4 Electrical Safety
- Portable electrical equipment shall be PAT tested annually. Stickers shall record the test date.
- Fixed installations shall be inspected by a qualified electrician every five years, or sooner if there is reason to doubt safety.
- No unauthorised modification of electrical circuits is permitted.

2.5 Lone Working
Grounds staff shall not operate machinery (e.g., mowers, strimmers, irrigation pumps) while alone on the premises outside normal club hours. A check-in procedure with the Facilities Manager or duty officer is required.

2.6 Accident Reporting
All accidents and near misses shall be recorded in the Accident Book (kept in the club office) and reported to the Facilities Manager. RIDDOR-reportable incidents shall be notified to the enforcing authority by the Facilities Manager within the statutory timescale.

5.3.2 Monthly (all courts)

- Inspect surface for cracks, lifting, or surface deterioration. Record any defects in the Exception Log with a photograph.

**5.8 Irrigation System**

**5.8.1 General**

The irrigation system serves the following areas: the main square, the practice nets, the bowling green surrounds, and the flower beds adjacent to the clubhouse. The system is a fully automated pop-up sprinkler system with a central controller located in the equipment store. Water is supplied from the mains via a dedicated metered connection.

The purpose of this section is to define the procedures for the seasonal startup and shutdown of the irrigation system, and to specify the routine maintenance required to keep the system in good working order. All work on the irrigation system shall be carried out by the Facilities Manager or an approved contractor. The Facilities Manager shall keep a record of all irrigation system work in the Facilities Log, including the date, the nature of the work, and the name of any contractor involved.

**5.8.2 Seasonal Startup – Spring**

The system shall be started up each year in April, or as soon as the risk of frost has passed. The Facilities Manager shall determine the appropriate date based on the weather forecast. The startup procedure shall be carried out as follows:

1.  **Inspect the controller.** Check that the controller is functioning correctly and that the battery back-up is in good condition. Replace the battery if necessary.
2.  **Open the main isolation valve.** The valve is located in the valve box adjacent to the equipment store. Open the valve slowly to avoid water hammer.
3.  **Pressurise the system.** Once the main valve is open, allow the system to pressurise. Check all visible pipework and connections for leaks.
4.  **Check the backflow preventer.** The backflow preventer shall be tested by an approved contractor at least once every two years. The test shall be recorded in the Facilities Log.
5.  **Inspect the sprinkler heads.** Walk the entire system and check each sprinkler head. Remove any debris, soil, or grass clippings from around the heads. Replace any damaged or missing heads.
6.  **Adjust the spray patterns.** Adjust the sprinkler heads so that they water the intended areas only. Avoid watering paths, fences, or the clubhouse building.
7.  **Set the controller programme.** Set the controller to the appropriate watering schedule for the time of year. The schedule shall be adjusted to account for rainfall. Watering shall not take place during periods of heavy rain.
8.  **Run a manual test.** Run each zone manually for a short period to confirm that the system is operating correctly. Check that each zone is pressurising and that the sprinkler heads are popping up and retracting properly.

**5.8.3 Seasonal Shutdown – Autumn**

The system shall be shut down each year in October, or as soon as the risk of frost is imminent. The Facilities Manager shall determine the appropriate date based on the weather forecast. The shutdown procedure shall be carried out as follows:

1.  **Drain the system.** The system is fitted with drain valves at the lowest points of the pipework. Open all drain valves and allow the system to drain completely.
2.  **Blow out the system.** Using an air compressor, blow out any remaining water from the pipework. This is essential to prevent frost damage to the pipes and sprinkler heads. The compressor shall be connected to the system via the drain valve fitting.
3.  **Close the main isolation valve.** Once the system is drained, close the main isolation valve.
4.  **Insulate exposed pipework.** Any pipework that is above ground and could be exposed to frost shall be insulated.
5.  **Protect the controller.** The controller shall be protected from damp and cold. The battery shall be removed and stored in a warm, dry place.
6.  **Record the shutdown.** The date of the shutdown shall be recorded in the Facilities Log.

**6.1 General Principles**

The procedures in this Section apply when there is an immediate risk to health and safety, a risk of significant damage to club property, or a failure that prevents the club from operating. In all cases, the safety of members, visitors, and staff takes precedence over the protection of buildings and equipment.

Where an emergency occurs outside normal working hours, the Facilities Manager shall be contacted in the first instance. If the Facilities Manager cannot be reached, the Club Secretary shall be contacted. The duty of any staff member or volunteer who discovers an emergency is to make the situation safe where it is safe to do so, and then to report the matter without delay.

The Facilities Manager shall maintain a list of approved contractors for emergency call-outs. This list is reproduced at Section 6.6. The list shall be reviewed annually and updated whenever a contractor's details change.

**6.2 Gas Leak or Suspected Gas Leak**

If a gas leak is suspected, or if there is a strong smell of gas in or near the clubhouse, the following procedure shall be followed:

1.  Do not operate any electrical switches, including light switches, and do not use a mobile phone inside the building.
2.  Open doors and windows to ventilate the area.
3.  Turn off the gas supply at the meter, if it is safe to do so. The meter is located in the external cupboard on the north wall of the clubhouse.
4.  Leave the building immediately.
5.  Telephone the National Gas Emergency Service on **0800 111 999**. Give the operator the club's address and postcode (The Pavilion, Green Lane, Melton Mowbray, LE13 0JZ) and state that the building is a sports clubhouse.
6.  Do not re-enter the building until it has been declared safe by the emergency service or a Gas Safe registered engineer.

**6.3 Fire**

All staff and volunteers shall be familiar with the fire evacuation procedure, which is displayed on the noticeboard in the main hall and in the kitchen. The procedure is summarised below.

1.  Raise the alarm by shouting "FIRE" and operating the nearest break-glass alarm point.
2.  Evacuate the building by the nearest available exit. Do not stop to collect personal belongings.
3.  Assemble at the designated assembly point, which is the far side of the car park, by the main gate.
4.  The Duty Officer or senior staff member present shall check that the building is clear, if it is safe to do so.
5.  Telephone the Fire Service on **999** from a safe location. State the address clearly.

**Resolved:** That Rajiv Nair be appointed as Clubhouse Maintenance Lead, with effect from 1 September 2021. A. Pendlebury to prepare an induction pack and handover notes by 15 September. Rajiv to be added to the club’s contractor and keyholder list and to the emergency contact rota.

**7. Any other business**

- J. Whitfield raised the condition of the car park surface. Several potholes have appeared near the entrance. The Committee agreed that this should be added to the 2020 maintenance plan. R. Bhatt will obtain quotations for patching and bring them to the October meeting.
- K. Lloyd reported that the clubhouse gas safety certificate is due for renewal on 30 November. The inspection will be arranged for mid-November to allow time for any remedial work.
- A. Pendlebury noted that the club’s annual fire risk assessment is overdue. The previous assessment was completed in September 2018. The Committee agreed to commission a new assessment before the end of October. A. Pendlebury to arrange this.

**8. Date of next meeting**
Tuesday, 8 October 2019, 19:30, Clubhouse Boardroom.

Meeting closed at 20:40.

**Facilities Committee Minutes**

**Meeting held Tuesday, 8 October 2019, 19:30, Clubhouse Boardroom**

**Present:** M. Okonkwo (Chair), K. Lloyd (Treasurer), A. Pendlebury (Grounds Lead), R. Bhatt, J. Whitfield, M. Hollis, S. Carter (Secretary)

**Apologies:** None.

---

**1. Minutes of the previous meeting**

The minutes of the meeting held on 10 September 2019 were approved as a correct record. Proposed by K. Lloyd, seconded by J. Whitfield.

**Matters arising:**

- The car park surface condition was discussed. R. Bhatt confirmed that two contractors have been approached for quotations for patching the potholes near the entrance. Written quotations are expected by the end of the week. R. Bhatt will circulate them to the Committee by email ahead of the next meeting.
- The clubhouse gas safety certificate renewal was confirmed as scheduled. A. Pendlebury reported that the inspection has been booked for 18 November with GasSafe registered engineer P. Okafor. The certificate is due to expire on 30 November.
- A. Pendlebury confirmed that the annual fire risk assessment has been commissioned. The assessment is scheduled for 28 October with FireCheck Associates. The report is expected within seven working days of the visit.

---

**2. Clubhouse Maintenance Lead – Handover Update**

A. Pendlebury reported that the handover to Rajiv Nair has progressed well. An induction pack has been prepared and a copy has been provided to the Secretary for the Committee file. The handover notes cover the following items:

- Fuse board replacement – scheduled for 14 October, contractor: Whitfield Electrical.
- Extractor fan repair – repair quote accepted; work scheduled for 21 October.
- Boiler service history and servicing schedule.
- Contractor contact list, including emergency out-of-hours numbers.
- Keyholder list and alarm codes.
- Cleaning schedule and supply ordering process.

Rajiv has been added to the club’s contractor and keyholder list and to the emergency contact rota. He has also been added to the club’s email distribution list for maintenance-related correspondence.

The Committee noted the update. A. Pendlebury will formally hand over all remaining maintenance files to Rajiv by 15 October.

---

**3. Budget Review – Maintenance Expenditure to 30 September 2019**

K. Lloyd presented a summary of maintenance expenditure for the financial year to date. The Committee noted the following items:

| Item | Budget | Actual to 30 Sep | Notes |
|------|--------|------------------|-------|
| Grounds maintenance (general) | £4,800 | £3,120 | Includes court repairs and strimming |
| Clubhouse repairs | £2,500 | £1,890 | Includes fuse board and extractor fan |
| Fire safety | £350 | £0 | Assessment booked for 28 October |
| Gas safety | £180 | £0 | Inspection booked for 18 November |
| Contingency | £1,000 | £0 | Unallocated |

K. Lloyd noted that expenditure is within budget. The Committee agreed that any unspent contingency at the year-end should be carried forward to the 2020 maintenance plan.

**Resolved:** That the maintenance budget position be noted, and that the unspent contingency be carried forward to 2020.

---

**4. Maintenance Plan – Proposed Changes for 2020**

A. Pendlebury presented a draft maintenance plan for 2020. The following items were discussed:

- **Car park patching:** To be added to the 2020 plan. R. Bhatt to bring quotations to the November meeting. Estimated cost: £1,200–£1,800 depending on the extent of patching required.
- **Court 2 surface inspection:** The surface was last inspected in March 2019. A. Pendlebury recommended a full inspection in spring 2020 to assess whether resurfacing will be required. The Committee agreed to include this as a provisional item.
- **Clubhouse redecoration:** Proposed for autumn 2020. The Committee agreed to include this as a provisional item, subject to budget availability.
- **Gutter cleaning and roof inspection:** Scheduled for spring 2020. This was previously carried out in April 2018.
